title: Every part of an item agrees
statement: An item's parts must agree: the stem asks for what the options offer, the key names an option that exists, and the explanation and feedback support that key.
example: An answer letter that disagreed with its explanation made 7 of 30 questions fail a cross-check by another model.
detail: In a 295-item run, 34 items failed the judge's factual-accuracy check while the pipeline's maths check reported 'math_errors_found: 0' (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/PASS_RATE_ANALYSIS.md`). The project's judged failures include a key contradicted by its own explanation (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/inceptbench_lambda/TRAINING_GUIDE.md`), a stem that asks for a model while only numeric answers are offered, and a key labelled 'A' on an item with no choices (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/FAILURE_PATTERN_ANALYSIS.md`). The explanation and feedback are written once the option order is fixed and tied to the options' wording rather than their letters, and they say why the common wrong choices are wrong. The agreement is checked in code.
against: In an earlier 257-item run the maths check and the judge agreed, with '- **Result:** ✅ All math is already correct!' and '- Math accuracy: 100% ✅' (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/archive/old_docs/gvc/GVC_FINAL_ARCHITECTURE.md`, lines 60 and 65); that run's failures were put down to format. the generator's first code check for the mismatch looked only at whether the key was called right or wrong, never at a wrong option called correct, and passed by default when it found neither. When code has proved the key right, the committed evaluator counts a mismatched explanation as a clarity fault, not a wrong fact: "This is a `clarity_precision` failure, NOT a `factual_accuracy` failure." (`icloud-work/incept/inceptbench/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/closed_ended_evaluation.txt`, line 99). It fits the record on feedback that sends the student back only once a student's attempts are over, since that record says feedback on a wrong answer never says what the student has to produce.
